title: The associated graded of a finite completed module is generated in degree zero
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}A/I^r$ its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $\widehat A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $I^nM=(I\widehat A)^nM$, with $I^0M=M$. Let $B=\operatorname{gr}_I(A)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ be the associated graded ring [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], with unit $1\bmod I$ in degree zero and multiplication $(a\bmod I^{n+1})(b\bmod I^{m+1})=ab\bmod I^{n+m+1}$, and the graded $B$-module $G=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^nM/I^{n+1}M$, whose action on homogeneous elements is $(a\bmod I^{m+1})(x\bmod I^{n+1}M)=ax\bmod I^{m+n+1}M$. Here direct sums consist of tuples of finite support, with componentwise addition and the displayed products extended distributively. Then $M/IM$ is a finitely generated $A/I$-module, and, for every finite family $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_t$ generating $M/IM$ over $A/I$, these elements, placed in degree zero, generate $G$ over $B$. Explicitly, for every $n\ge0$ and $y\in I^nM$, and any lifts $x_j\in M$ of $\bar x_j$, there exist $a_1,\ldots,a_t\in I^n$ such that $y-\sum_{j=1}^ta_jx_j\in I^{n+1}M$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Z (label lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), proof lines 6621-6630: the affine algebraic assertion; tags/tags confirms 087Z,coherent-lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra. The quotient of completion used here is Algebra 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2).

proof.text: *The objects.* $I\widehat A$ is the ideal of $\widehat A$ generated by the image of $I$ under $\iota:A\to\widehat A$, and $(I\widehat A)^n=I^n\widehat A$ is generated by $\iota(I^n)$. $B$ is the ring $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. The action on $G$ is well defined: for $a\in I^m$ and $x\in I^nM$ we have $ax\in I^{m+n}M$, and replacing $a$ by $a+a'$ with $a'\in I^{m+1}$, or $x$ by $x+x'$ with $x'\in I^{n+1}M$, changes $ax$ by $a'x+ax'+a'x'\in I^{m+n+1}M$. Associativity, unit and distributivity are inherited from those of $M$ over $\widehat A$.

proof.text: *$M/IM$ is finite over $A/I$, and $\widehat A=\iota(A)+I\widehat A$.* Since $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (2) the map $\pi:\widehat A\to A/I$, $(x_r)_r\mapsto x_1$, is surjective with kernel $I\widehat A$ and $\pi\circ\iota$ is the quotient map $A\to A/I$; so $\widehat A/I\widehat A\cong A/I$ as $A$-algebras. Hence for $b\in\widehat A$, choosing $c\in A$ with $c\bmod I=\pi(b)$, we get $b-\iota(c)\in\ker\pi=I\widehat A$, i.e. $\widehat A=\iota(A)+I\widehat A$. If $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ generate $M$ over $\widehat A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], their images generate $M/IM$ over $\widehat A/I\widehat A$, hence over $A/I$ through the isomorphism (the $A/I$-module structure on $M/IM$ is the one through $\iota$, since $\pi\circ\iota$ is the quotient map). This is the first assertion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, algebra.tex line 22645), 'R^/I^nR^ = R/I^n' for n = 1

proof.text: *Reduction to $A$-modules.* Regard $M$ as an $A$-module through $\iota$, and for an ideal $J\subseteq A$ let $J\cdot M$ be the $A$-submodule generated by the $am$, $a\in J$, $m\in M$. Then $(J\widehat A)M=J\cdot M$: an element of $J\widehat A$ is $\sum_k\iota(a_k)b_k$ with $a_k\in J$, $b_k\in\widehat A$, and $(\sum_k\iota(a_k)b_k)m=\sum_ka_k(b_km)$; conversely $am=\iota(a)m$. With $J=I^n$ this gives $I^nM=(I\widehat A)^nM=I^n\cdot M$ for all $n\ge0$ ($I^0=A$, $I^0M=M$). Let $f:A^{\oplus t}\to M$, $(c_j)\mapsto\sum_jc_jx_j$, an $A$-linear map. Then $M=f(A^{\oplus t})+I\cdot M$: for $m\in M$ write $m\bmod IM=\sum_j\bar c_j\bar x_j$ with $\bar c_j\in A/I$ (step 2), lift $\bar c_j$ to $c_j\in A$; then $m-\sum_jc_jx_j\in IM=I\cdot M$. Finally $I^n\cdot A^{\oplus t}=(I^n)^{\oplus t}$, the tuples with all entries in $I^n$.

proof.text: *The congruence.* Let $n\ge0$ and $y\in I^nM=I^n\cdot M$ (step 3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-graded-lift-mod-ideal-power] to $R=A$, the ideal $I$ and the $A$-linear map $f:A^{\oplus t}\to M$ of step 3, whose hypothesis $M=f(A^{\oplus t})+I\cdot M$ is step 3. It gives $x=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)\in I^n\cdot A^{\oplus t}=(I^n)^{\oplus t}$, so $a_j\in I^n$, with $\sum_ja_jx_j-y\in I^{n+1}\cdot M=I^{n+1}M$. This is the explicit assertion, for any choice of lifts $x_j$. For $n=0$ it reads: every $y\in M$ is $\sum_ja_jx_j$ modulo $IM$ with $a_j\in A$, which is the generation of $M/IM$ by the $\bar x_j$ again.

proof.text: *Generation in degree zero.* An element of $G$ is a finite sum of homogeneous elements $y\bmod I^{n+1}M$ with $y\in I^nM$. By step 4 and the definition of the action (step 1), $y\bmod I^{n+1}M=\sum_j(a_j\bmod I^{n+1})\cdot(x_j\bmod IM)=\sum_j(a_j\bmod I^{n+1})\cdot\bar x_j$ with $a_j\bmod I^{n+1}\in B_n$. So the $\bar x_j$, in degree zero, generate $G$ over $B$.

lean.statement: theorem completedModule_associatedGraded_generators {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (AdicCompletion I A) M] [Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) M] : letI : Module A M := Module.compHom M (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A)) Module.Finite (A ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule A M)) ∧ (∀ (t : ℕ) (xbar : Fin t → M ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule A M)), Submodule.span (A ⧸ I) (Set.range xbar) = ⊤ → ∀ (x : Fin t → M), (∀ j, Submodule.Quotient.mk (x j) = xbar j) → ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : M), y ∈ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) → ∃ (b : Fin t → Ideal.associatedGradedPiece I n) (a : Fin t → (I ^ n : Ideal A)), (∀ j, b j = Submodule.Quotient.mk (a j)) ∧ y - ∑ j, (a j : A) • x j ∈ (I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A M)))
lean.note: The explicit representative formulation of both conclusions. Finite generation over A/I is expressed by finitely many lifts spanning modulo IM; homogeneous coefficients b_j in the recorded associated graded pieces are supplied together with representatives a_j in I^n. The degreewise congruence is equivalent to generation of the finite-support direct sum over gr_I(A).
